analysis:
The change is confined to the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Prompting/GLM5NextPromptPolicyTests.swift. It adds no production code and no new attack surface. The head hunks extend fixtures for the GLM5 native prompt-policy RawControls and thinking-control validation:
- Head lines 143-146 add no-op controls: thinking {type: enabled}, thinking: true, null siblings, and reasoning with a null max_tokens/exclude and summary "auto".
- Lines 216-217 add Anthropic-style thinking-off spellings.
- Lines 236-237 add contradictory thinking-vs-reasoning cases that must be refused.
- Line 310 changes the malformed sibling from summary:auto to mode:pro, because summary "auto" is now accepted.
- Lines 488-497 move thinking:true, null preserve_thinking, thinking:"enabled", adaptive, budget_tokens, reasoning:true, summary:verbose, summary:true, generate_summary and context into the fail-closed malformed list.
These tests assert fail-closed behavior: malformed, contradictory and exclusion controls are refused on both the coordinator and local-HTTP paths. They also assert that the 400 error carries a fixed message that never crosses to the coordinator (lines 352-367).
The production RawControls parser change is not in the supplied batch. The tests presuppose it, and I could not verify its accuracy. Nothing here touches the threat-model assets: keys, attestation, encryption, the prefix cache T-041, authorization or billing. The one residual question is whether the production parser treats the newly accepted null and thinking spellings consistently with the prompt-cache scope and render determinism. That is outside this test-only diff. The patch excerpt and the head text past line 508 were truncated, and the new ThinkFixture lines 645-807 were not supplied. No findings.
